mechanism_narrative: A declining federal funds rate signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces the cost of capital for corporations, leading to higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS is declining (measured over 12-month rolling windows), or the Rank IC falls below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate exceeds 5.0%, it signals a weakening labor market that reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when UNRATE > 5.0%, or the Rank IC is below 0.02 over any 12-month rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in the federal funds rate and unemployment rate indicate a tightening monetary policy coinciding with a deteriorating labor market, which signals economic slowdown and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increase > 0.1% and UNRATE increase > 0.1% over 3 months
regime_hint: monetary tightening with labor market weakness
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when both FEDFUNDS and UNRATE are rising (by >0.1% each), or the Rank IC for the interaction signal is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: In the post-pandemic housing recovery phase, rising new housing starts (HOUST) signal strong consumer confidence and economic expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods during the post-pandemic housing recovery phase, or the Rank IC falls below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: A rising industrial production index (INDPRO) indicates robust manufacturing activity and economic growth, which supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO is rising, or the Rank IC is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: When the year-over-year CPI inflation rate exceeds 5.0%, it signals persistent inflation that may trigger aggressive monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when CPIAUCSL YoY change > 5.0%, or the Rank IC is below 0.02 over any 12-month rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in new housing starts (HOUST) and industrial production (INDPRO) indicate strong demand and supply chain resilience, which signals robust economic growth and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increase > 0.5% and INDPRO increase > 0.5% over 3 months
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when both HOUST and INDPRO are rising (by >0.5% each), or the Rank IC for the interaction signal is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: In the context of a strong labor market recovery, sustained growth in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) above 200,000 (thousands) per month signals rising employment and consumer spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when PAYEMS growth exceeds 200,000 (thousands per month) during the strong labor market recovery phase, or the Rank IC is below 0.02.
